Guidance & outlook: But what we are trying to say is we expect through the Roha plant and the ong oing Ankleshwar plant, that we are aspiring to take 10% of the global resin volume, which I think is a fairly big aspiration from that perspective.
After these works, total resin capacity across the two sites is expected to reach approximately 5x the capacity that existed before construction of the Roha plant.
Across these three businesses, our order book stood at INR 2,473 crores as of June 2026, providing healthy execution visibility.
Growth & demand: Overall, the plan is to have a 3x business growth over the years.
Now that we are reporting these number segments separately, but a very, very positive, healthy 21% growth in CAGR over the year of the last 4 years.
In addition, the bid pipeline stood at INR 9,777 crores, providing a strong opportunity funnel for future order inflows.
Margins & costs: The EBITDA margin stood at 4.54%, and net profit was INR 3 crores, while the PAT margin was 0.44%.
The segment EBIT margin increased by 145% to INR 13 crores , while EBIT margin improved significantly to 11.89% from less than 6% in the corresponding quarter of last year.
EBIT margin was 9.92% as compared with 10.55% in the previous year , Primarily reflecting higher input cost.
Capex & expansion: We have all been talking about the Roha facility, where we have shown a picture earlier, which is another part of the plant, where the capacity expansion for our flagship business, the ion exchange resins, has increased by 5x through the setting up of the Roha plant, which is currently commissioned and going through stabilization and ongoing production incre…
So, clearly, Roha gives us technology leadership, circular manufacturing, a 5x capacity expansion, and future-ready operations.
Our pharma resin factory is FDA approved, and the capacity expansion plan is 6x.
Balance sheet & cash: And the team continues to work to see that the full potential of growth and opportunities that exist in the South Europe, Iberian market, as well as in the North African market, which can be catered to also from that entity are fully leveraged.
Having said that, we do not want to increase our exposure as a company to more receivables unless and until the funds flow happen.
In terms of the exposures on the accounts receivable, we don't call out separately on the contract specific details.
Risks & challenges: The company is also geared up to offer solutions in semi-conductor as well as for data centers with cooling water treatment solutions, high efficiency RO and softening systems, and also looking at technologies like direct liquid cooling.
And there also, it will help us expand our product portfolio with the new weak acid cation and the acrylic anion resin grades.
The EBITDA stood at INR 32 crores, which declined by 49% year-on- year.

Guidance & outlook: As at 31st March '26, the engineering order book stood at INR 26,433 million, providing healthy revenue visibility going forward.
Our guidance has been in the past that we will work towards 25% capacity utilization of the Roha plant in the first full year of operation.

Apart from that, our order intake has been quite healthy; in fact, it has been 40% more than the last full financial year, and we expect a majority of those projects to get executed in this financial year and the next.
Growth & demand: The enquiry pipeline continues to remain healthy with both quarter-on- quarter and year-on year growth in order inflows, driven primarily by medium-sized opportunities across sectors.
This segment continues to witness healthy volume growth supported by expanding market reach and increasing product acceptance.
As we've said in previous calls, we continue to invest for growth in this segment, and our efforts are showing results: the division has grown 34% year-on-year.
Margins & costs: The EBITDA stood at INR 199 million and EBITDA margin stood at 2.31% and net profit was INR 243 million and the PAT margin was at 2.81%.
EBITDA stood at INR 2,102 million, down 29% year-on-year.
The EBITDA margin stood at 7.21%, and the net profit was INR 1,432 million, whilst the PAT margin was at 4.91%.
Capex & expansion: During the quarter, we achieved an important milestone with the successful commissioning of the raw water treatment plant for the IOCL Panipat Refinery project, which is the largest industrial water treatment package awarded in India.
The CAPEX is around USD 40 million over the next two years, and we'll be funding it with a mix of debt and equity.
At this juncture, the CAPEX what we have envisaged is more into the maintenance and routine CAPEX, which is in the region of around Rs.30 to 40 crores.
Balance sheet & cash: As mentioned earlier, the project will be funded by a mix of debt and equity.
And in terms of the gross debt, presently it is in the region of Rs.384 crores.
Harsh Shah Just to carry forward from the previous participant, sir, so you told that the maintenance and routine CAPEX for FY27 will be Rs.30-40 crores and gross debt will be around Rs.384 crores.
Risks & challenges: During the quarter, planned dispatches of certain high-value engineering contracts to the GCC geographies were impacted due to disruptions arising from the West Asia crisis.
However, the turnover was impacted primarily in March '26 due to logistic disruption from the West Asia crisis.

We continue to remain in line with those expectations While there are near term headwinds related to the West Asia crisis - notably higher costs for certain critical raw materials such as styrene and oleum - we believe these risks will be mitigated over time.
